result: 1. [CRITICAL] Frame-time spikes on level-2: p95 51.44ms vs 16.7ms budget

lines.text: Root cause is clear: 800 meshes per pickup, each with its own geometry + material, never removed or disposed. Baseline now: load level-2, two pickups, measure 8s.

gamedog_annotate(note: "agent: confetti → single InstancedMesh ring-buffer pool …")

I fixed the top finding, the level-2 frame-time spikes. It was critical and hit 84.9% of sessions: 74% of hitches came within 1.5s of a `powerup` event, and the `particles` gauge sat at 1,600.

**Cause:** every tennis-ball pickup (`confettiBurst` in `apps/zoomies/src/fx.js`) created 800 separate meshes. Each had its own `SphereGeometry` and `MeshStandardMaterial`, cast shadows, and was never removed from the scene or freed. They even carried over between levels, which explains the 3,200 particles on level-3.

**Fix:** all the confetti is now one `InstancedMesh` with a single shared low-poly geometry and material. It reuses a fixed set of 1,600 slots, so a burst creates no new objects. Pieces shrink out and expire after 2.2s. The motion and colours are the same as before. One thing looks different: pieces now shrink away instead of fading out, and they're 20-sided low-poly shapes instead of smooth spheres. `GAME_VERSION` is now `1.0.1` in `apps/zoomies/src/version.js`.

**Live measurement.** Both runs used the same steps from a fresh page with no confetti: load level-2, trigger 2 pickups, measure for 8s.

| | Before (1.0.0) | After (1.0.1) |
|---|---|---|
| Draw calls (avg) | 3,494 | 296 |
| Triangles (avg) | 1,176,661 | 67,837 |
| CPU time per frame for rendering, p95 | 9.98 ms | 1.3 ms |
| Worst frame | 50 ms | 16.8 ms |
| Frames over budget | 0.2% | 0% |
| Confetti still in the scene afterwards | 1,600, never freed | 0 (all expired) |

Frame-time p95 read 16.78 ms both times. This machine runs at a capped 60fps, so p95 can't show the gain here. The players who will feel it are on slower GPUs, where production p95 on level-2 was 51 ms. The measurement can't see the frames where the bursts were created, because pickups can't be triggered while a measurement is running. So the 50 ms → 16.8 ms worst-frame result covers the time after the bursts, not the spawn moment itself.

I added a note to the session describing the change and these numbers. Nothing is committed.

**What's left:**
- Once players have played 1.0.1, run `gamedog_compare_versions` (or open Versions in the dashboard) and look at level-2 and level-3 p95 and the low-tier GPU numbers. Triage already lists 5 sessions as 1.0.1, probably from earlier testing, so they'll be mixed in until real traffic outweighs them.
- Level geometry still grows on every level load (finding #5, renderer geometries reached 1,152 during this test). It's a separate issue I didn't touch.
- The `spawnScorePopup` TypeError (finding #3) is also still there.
